neighbours.label: ironic understatement in a casual, humorous narrative voice ('let's just say ... will not be', 'a little shaky', 'a pretty apt description')
fire: Let's just say my first attempt at baking bread was not a roaring success.
The hotel pool was, shall we say, a little smaller than the photos suggested.
My brother's singing at the wedding was not exactly what you'd call music.
Calling that hike a gentle stroll would be a slight understatement, trust me.
Let's just say the cat was less than thrilled about her first bath.
The dog's obedience class did not go entirely according to plan, I admit.
Our camping trip was, to put it mildly, a little damp this year.
I wouldn't say the new boss is the warmest person I've ever met.
quiet: My first attempt at baking bread turned out dense and slightly burnt.
The hotel pool was smaller than the photos suggested, about ten metres long.
My brother sang two songs at the wedding and everyone clapped along.
The hike took four hours and climbed about eight hundred metres in total.
The cat hissed and scratched me during her first bath last night.
The dog's obedience class finished early because the trainer was ill.
Our camping trip had three days of rain and one sunny afternoon this year.
The new boss is strict and rarely smiles during our weekly meetings.

notes: card: no single token; peaks on ' little', ' not', ' pretty', "'t" in jokey understatement in dialogue and blogs. Probe: 'Let's just say the soup was not the highlight' 0.50; a sincere 'a little nervous' line 0.07. Near misses keep the casual topics but state things plainly.
